question_text: Evaluate lim(x → 0) (aˣ − 1)/(bˣ − 1), where a > 0, b > 0 and b ≠ 1.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you divide by and what the standard limit lim(x → 0) (aˣ − 1)/x equals.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Divide above and below by x
steps.margin_note: First mark. The same standard limit is used twice, once with a and once with b. Quote it before substituting either letter.
lines: For x ≠ 0 divide the numerator and the denominator by x.
(dividing the top and the bottom by x ≠ 0 does not

recall.must_convey: That both parts are divided by x so that the standard limit lim(x → 0) (aˣ − 1)/x = logₑa can be used on each.
accept: divide the top and the bottom by x and use a to the x minus one over x is log a
the same standard limit is used with a and then with b
both go to zero so divide each by x first
x tho divide cheste rendu standard limits avuthayi
quote the a to the x minus one over x formula
heard_as: a to the x minus one

steps.why: The denominator is also 0 at x = 0, so the standard limit cannot be applied to the fraction as it stands. Dividing both parts by x makes each one an instance of the same known limit.
common_mistakes: Cancelling the −1 in the numerator against the −1 in the denominator.
Writing the answer as aˣ/bˣ or as a/b.
steps.memory_tip: One formula covers both lines: lim (aˣ − 1)/x = logₑa. Read the base, write its natural logarithm.

steps.label: Take the ratio of the two logarithms
steps.margin_note: Second mark. b ≠ 1 is what makes logₑb ≠ 0, so the quotient rule for limits may be used. The answer is also written as the logarithm of a to the base b, by the change-of-base rule.
lines: Since b ≠ 1, logₑb ≠ 0, so the limit of the quotient
is the quotient of the limits.

recall.must_convey: That the answer is logₑa divided by logₑb, which is log to the base b of a.
accept: log a divided by log b
the answer is log a by log b to the base e
it is log of a to the base b
log a by log b vasthundi
the ratio of the two natural logarithms

steps.why: b ≠ 1 is stated in the question exactly so that logₑb is not 0 and the division is allowed. The value checks numerically: with a = 4 and b = 2 the answer is logₑ4/logₑ2 = 2, and at x = 0.00001 the expression is 2.000007.
common_mistakes: Writing logₑ(a/b) instead of logₑa / logₑb.
Leaving out the condition b ≠ 1 that keeps the denominator non-zero.
steps.memory_tip: A ratio of two natural logarithms is a change of base: logₑa / logₑb is the logarithm of a to the base b. That is the compact form of the answer.
lines_compact: Since b ≠ 1, logₑb ≠ 0, so the limit of the quotient
is the quotient of the limits.

insider_note: Divide top and bottom by x so each becomes the standard (aˣ − 1)/x → logₑa. The condition b ≠ 1 is what keeps logₑb from being zero, so it belongs in the answer.
